num_tasks: int, total number of tasks n; tasks use 1-based numbering 1…n, and every task-indexed list stores the data of task i at position i-1.
processing_times: list[int], length must be num_tasks; processing_times[i-1] is the positive integer processing time of task i, in the same unit as cycle_time.
cycle_time: int, positive integer cycle time C; the maximum total task processing time any station can accommodate, in the same unit as processing_times.
num_stations: int, fixed number of stations m; stations use 1-based numbering 1…m. This value is the instance-given minimum feasible number of stations, not a variable to be optimized.
precedence_arcs: list[list[int]], list of immediate precedence arcs; each element is strictly [predecessor, successor], both numbered 1…num_tasks, meaning the station number of the predecessor task must not be greater than the station number of the successor task. An empty list means there are no precedence arcs.
earliest_stations: list[int], length must be num_tasks; earliest_stations[i-1] is the earliest station number E_i to which task i can be assigned, using 1-based station numbering and inclusive of that endpoint.
latest_stations: list[int], length must be num_tasks; latest_stations[i-1] is the latest station number L_i to which task i can be assigned, using 1-based station numbering and inclusive of that endpoint; must satisfy earliest_stations[i-1] ≤ latest_stations[i-1].
